assumptions: The bridge from potential client-side code execution to local unprivileged execution on the same host is an inference, never a fact.
The source and target products are co-deployed on the same Windows host only as an unverified condition.

evidence_quotes.quote: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI
allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file

missing_conditions: The victim visits or loads the relevant remote web page in an affected Oculus Browser version.
The HTML injection results in actual code execution rather than only UI spoofing; the source description says execution is only potentially possible.
The resulting execution occurs in a local unprivileged user context.
The Oculus Browser and vulnerable Oculus Desktop installation are deployed on the same host.
The host is Windows and runs the affected Oculus Desktop version.
The privileged OVRRedir.exe process, unprivileged log-file write condition, and hard-link exploitation conditions are present.
The resulting local user context can perform the target CVE's required local actions.
Environment evidence confirming these conditions is absent.
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 describes arbitrary HTML injection into the Oculus Browser UI and potentially executing code from a remote web page; it does not establish actual execution, a local user context, or execution on a host running Oculus Desktop. CVE-2020-1885 requires a local user on Windows with the vulnerable Oculus Desktop and its privileged OVRRedir.exe, unprivileged-file, and hard-link conditions, and describes gaining privileges rather than specifically SYSTEM-level escalation. The edge claim therefore overstates both the source postcondition and the target result. The causal bridge is plausible only conditionally and cannot enter a strict graph as a supported edge without verification of the listed prerequisites.
